title: Synergistic hydrogen sulfide mitigation in sour crude oil using green‐synthesized copper nanoparticles and chemical scavengers
content:
Abstract

Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) in sour crude oil poses significant operational, environmental, and safety challenges due to its toxicity and corrosive properties. This study examined the preliminary performance of green-synthesized copper nanoparticles (CuNPs), prepared using Biebersteinia multifida root extract, as an additional treatment alongside the commercial H2S scavenger MAKS 9185. Laboratory batch experiments used 250 mL crude-oil samples with an initial estimated H2S concentration of 915 ppm. The commercial scavenger was applied at a fixed nominal dosage, while the CuNP preparation was added at volumetric ratios of 0.8% to 12.8% relative to the initial crude-oil volume. Residual H2S concentrations were estimated using a Dräger-based measurement procedure after a prescribed 30-min settling period. Treatment with the scavenger alone reduced the estimated H2S concentration to 15 ppm, yielding a calculated removal efficiency of 98.36%. Adding the CuNP preparation at a nominal dosage of 4.8% resulted in a lower reported residual concentration of 3 ppm, equivalent to a calculated removal efficiency of 99.67%. This was an 80% reduction in residual H2S compared with the scavenger-only treatment. Increasing the nominal CuNP preparation dosage to 12.8% produced no further measurable improvement. These findings offer preliminary evidence that combining plant-mediated copper nanoparticle preparations with a commercial chemical scavenger may further reduce residual H2S under laboratory conditions. However, independent experimental replication, analytical validation, component-specific controls, and quantitative evaluation of copper recovery and process feasibility are needed before the treatment's reproducibility, mechanisms, and practical advantages can be confirmed.
